question: Under tail-degree shift on citation graphs, does adding a single degree-aware L2 scaling parameter to a tuned 2-layer GCN improve macro-F1 over the unmodified baseline and match or beat a 4-module stack?
target_scope: Semi-supervised node classification under prespecified degree-shift splits
unit_of_analysis: Fixed training-seed run over the held-out degree-shift test fold
construct_or_estimand: Macro-F1 difference between tuned 2-layer GCN, 1-parameter degree scaling, and 4-module stack across 5 seeds
measurement: Macro-F1 on frozen degree-shift test split with SHA-256 verified split manifest
prior_art_boundary: Prior work stacks 4 modules without reporting the 1-parameter degree-scaling ablation
rival_explanation: Extra attention and contrastive modules are unnecessary; either the 2-layer baseline matches them or 1-parameter scaling suffices
expected_if_focal: Single-parameter degree scaling improves macro-F1 by >=0.030 over tuned 2-layer GCN and matches or beats the 4-module stack
expected_if_rival: Tuned 2-layer GCN matches both single-parameter scaling and the 4-module stack within 0.005 macro-F1
discriminating_test: 5-seed matched-budget comparison of tuned 2-layer GCN, 1-parameter degree scaling, and 4-module stack
falsifying_result: Single-parameter scaling fails to beat tuned 2-layer GCN by >=0.015 macro-F1 under matched tuning budget
indeterminate_result: Engineering checks fail or seed variance interval spans both >=0.015 gain and 0 gain
pilot: Verify split disjointness, deterministic seed hashes, and 1-seed baseline parity before full 5-seed run
engineering_diagnosis: All 6 data-identity, split, preprocessing, metric, baseline-fidelity, and reference-reproduction checks passed
prior_outcome_exposure: No held-out outcomes inspected prior to frozen protocol
